16899.title: Clearing Denominators
16899.heading: Clearing Denominators
16899.content:
Clearing denominators multiplies every term on both sides of an equation by a common multiple of the denominators. Using the least common multiple usually keeps coefficients smallest.

The method converts a fractional equation into an equivalent form without fractions. Every term must receive the multiplier, including constants and terms outside visible fractions. Denominators containing variables require restrictions because the multiplier may be zero at excluded values. [[Cross Multiplication]] is a compact special case for an equation consisting of one fraction on each side.

16902.title: Clean-Room Semiconductor Manufacturing
16902.heading: Clean-Room Semiconductor Manufacturing
16902.content:
A semiconductor clean room filters air and controls contamination because tiny particles can ruin microscopic circuit features. Workers wear protective garments and follow tightly documented procedures.

Missile reliability programs helped institutionalize this discipline. Traceable production records allow defective batches to be identified and removed when later tests reveal a problem.

16905.title: Classifier
16905.heading: Classifier
16905.content:
A classifier is a computational system that assigns an observation to one of several classes. During [[Supervised Learning]], labeled examples teach the system a relationship between input features and desired categories.

A simple artificial neuron can classify two linearly separable groups by learning a [[Decision Boundary]]. A multiclass network can use a [[Softmax Function]] to output a probability for every class and select the class with the strongest result.

16908.title: CLASSIT
16908.heading: CLASSIT
16908.content:
CLASSIT extends COBWEB-style conceptual clustering so numerical as well as nominal attributes can be represented. Numeric values are summarized through distribution parameters rather than treated as unrelated categories.

The extension retains incremental probabilistic hierarchy construction while addressing the original method's restriction to nominal attributes.

16910.sourceSearchName: classifier ensemble matrix classifier ensemble matrix
16910.title: Classifier Ensemble Matrix
16910.heading: Document

16911.sourceSearchName: classifier ensemble matrix classifier ensemble matrix
16911.title: Classifier Ensemble Matrix
16911.heading: Classifier Ensemble Matrix
16911.content:
A classifier ensemble matrix visualizes the predictions or errors of multiple classifiers across many observations. Rows and columns align models, cases, labels, or confidence so that agreement and disagreement become visible patterns.

Sorting and linked views can reveal redundant classifiers, difficult cases, and complementary error regions. The matrix is most informative when the visual encoding distinguishes correct consensus from unanimous shared failure.

16912.sourceSearchName: classifier ensemble matrix classifier ensemble matrix
16912.title: Classifier Ensemble Matrix
16912.heading: References

16914.title: Classification
16914.heading: Classification
16914.content:
Classification assigns an observation to one of a set of discrete classes. A model is learned or specified from known data and then used to predict the class label of a new case.

When labels are supplied during learning, the task is supervised. Clustering differs because it attempts to discover the groups themselves.

16916.sourceSearchName: classification validation scheme classification validation scheme
16916.title: Classification Validation Scheme
16916.heading: Document

16917.sourceSearchName: classification validation scheme classification validation scheme
16917.title: Classification Validation Scheme
16917.heading: Classification Validation Scheme
16917.content:
A classification validation scheme determines which observations train a model and which independently test its predictions. Holdout, k-fold cross-validation, repeated splits, leave-one-out procedures, and bootstrap methods make different bias, variance, and computational tradeoffs.

The split must preserve relevant class and feature distributions without leaking test information into fitting. A performance measure is meaningful only relative to the sampling and reuse pattern that produced it.

16918.sourceSearchName: classification validation scheme classification validation scheme
16918.title: Classification Validation Scheme
16918.heading: References

16920.title: Classification Prediction
16920.heading: Classification Prediction
16920.content:
Classification prediction assigns an observation to one of a finite set of categories, such as popular versus unpopular or interested versus uninterested. The result is evaluated by comparing predicted and actual classes.

A [[Confusion Matrix]] separates correct and incorrect outcomes for each class. Accuracy alone can mislead on imbalanced data, so positive-class precision, recall, specificity, and their combined score may also be needed.

16922.sourceSearchName: classification permutation test classification permutation test
16922.title: Classification Permutation Test
16922.heading: Document

16923.sourceSearchName: classification permutation test classification permutation test
16923.title: Classification Permutation Test
16923.heading: Classification Permutation Test
16923.content:
A classification permutation test evaluates a performance difference against a null distribution generated by exchangeable rearrangements. Depending on the design, labels or paired classifier outcomes are permuted while the comparison statistic is recomputed.

The method avoids relying on a parametric sampling distribution whose assumptions may fail across datasets. Validity depends on permuting only units that are exchangeable under the null and repeating the entire relevant evaluation procedure.

16924.sourceSearchName: classification permutation test classification permutation test
16924.title: Classification Permutation Test
16924.heading: References

16926.title: Classification Nomogram
16926.heading: Classification Nomogram
16926.content:
A classification nomogram displays how predictor values contribute to a class score or probability along aligned scales. A reader traces an observation's values, accumulates their contributions, and maps the total to the prediction.

The form is especially useful for additive models because it exposes both direction and magnitude of each feature's effect. Complex interactions are harder to represent without losing the nomogram's direct readability.

16928.sourceSearchName: classification model evaluation classification model evaluation
16928.title: Classification Model Evaluation
16928.heading: Document

16929.sourceSearchName: classification model evaluation classification model evaluation
16929.title: Classification Model Evaluation
16929.heading: Classification Model Evaluation
16929.content:
Classification model evaluation tests whether a fitted classifier is accurate, reliable, and valid beyond the records used to construct it. A pilot or held-out test set can be temporarily treated as unseen data and then compared with its known labels.

Evaluation should reflect the intended application and class costs. A high training score alone can conceal overfitting.

16930.title: Classification Model Evaluation
16930.heading: References

16931.sourceSearchName: classification model construction classification model construction
16931.title: Classification Model Construction
16931.heading: Document

16932.sourceSearchName: classification model construction classification model construction
16932.title: Classification Model Construction
16932.heading: Classification Model Construction
16932.content:
Classification model construction fits rules, a tree, or a probability model to labeled training records. Each record is assumed to belong to a known class through its target label.

The construction algorithm determines which attributes, splits, or parameters represent the relationship. Its output must be evaluated independently before use on new data.

The book turns construction into a repeatable pipeline: define inputs and target, fit on the training partition, inspect the learned structure, and preserve the preprocessing rules required for later scoring. Construction is kept distinct from validation and final testing.

16933.sourceSearchName: classification model construction classification model construction
16933.title: Classification Model Construction
16933.heading: References

16934.sourceSearchName: classification model application classification model application
16934.title: Classification Model Application
16934.heading: Document

16935.sourceSearchName: classification model application classification model application
16935.title: Classification Model Application
16935.heading: Classification Model Application
16935.content:
Classification model application uses an evaluated model to assign labels to unseen records. A decision tree follows attribute branches, while a probabilistic classifier compares class probabilities.

Application also creates evidence about drift and failure. Predictions should be monitored because the data distribution and class meanings can change after deployment.

The book applies a fitted classifier to validation and test partitions using the same variables, encodings, and transformations learned during preparation. Returned probabilities support threshold-dependent measures and ranking displays in addition to class labels.

16936.sourceSearchName: classification model application classification model application
16936.title: Classification Model Application
16936.heading: References

16938.title: Classification Likelihood
16938.heading: Classification Likelihood
16938.content:
Classification likelihood evaluates a model while treating component assignments as part of the clustering solution. It rewards parameter values and memberships that jointly explain the observations.

This differs from mixture likelihood, which integrates over uncertain component membership. The choice affects how strongly the procedure favors crisp assignments.

16941.title: Classification Accuracy
16941.heading: Classification Accuracy
16941.content:
Classification accuracy is the proportion of evaluated cases whose predicted labels match their known labels. It provides a direct benchmark when every error is treated equally.

Accuracy can be misleading with imbalanced classes or unequal error costs. Reliability and validity require examining the evaluation design and the kinds of mistakes, not only the overall percentage.

16944.title: Classed Choropleth
16944.heading: Classed Choropleth
16944.content: A classed choropleth groups numeric observations into intervals and assigns one color to each class. Classes simplify the map and make a small number of spatial patterns easy to identify, but observations on opposite sides of a boundary appear more different than nearby values within a class. The [[Choropleth Class Count]] and classification rule must therefore be disclosed in the legend.

16947.title: Class Prediction
16947.heading: Class Prediction
16947.content:
Class prediction assigns a categorical label to a new observation from its measured features. An ideal rule chooses the class with the largest conditional probability for the observed predictor vector.

Because the true conditional probabilities are unknown, an algorithm estimates a decision rule from a [[Training Dataset]]. Performance must then be measured on held-out observations, since accurate classification of the training data can result from [[Overfitting]].

16950.title: Class Label
16950.heading: Class Label
16950.content:
A class label is a value representing the category to which an observation belongs. In supervised classification, the [[Training Dataset]] pairs every input example with the label the model is expected to predict.

Labels may be encoded as numbers even when they stand for human-readable classes. An image-recognition system can associate ten output positions with ten clothing categories, and a [[Softmax Function]] assigns a probability to each labeled possibility.

16952.sourceSearchName: class association rule class association rule
16952.title: Class Association Rule
16952.heading: Document

16953.sourceSearchName: class association rule class association rule
16953.title: Class Association Rule
16953.heading: Class Association Rule
16953.content:
A class association rule is an association whose consequent is restricted to a class label. Its antecedent is a set of attribute-value conditions, while support and confidence summarize how often the pattern occurs and how reliably it implies the class.

Restricting the consequent turns pattern mining into a source of predictive rules. Minimum support can miss useful rare-class patterns, so thresholds and class-sensitive weighting require deliberate selection.

16954.sourceSearchName: class association rule class association rule
16954.title: Class Association Rule
16954.heading: References

16956.title: Clarification Question
16956.heading: Clarification Question
16956.content:
A clarification question asks the user to distinguish among interpretations or supply a missing value. It converts uncertainty inside the assistant into a focused next turn.

Good clarification presents only the distinctions needed to proceed and preserves values already understood. It is a core recovery action in a [[Dialog Policy]], especially when [[Candidate Hypothesis Ranking]] leaves close alternatives.

16959.title: CKAN Resource
16959.heading: CKAN Resource
16959.content:
A CKAN resource is an individual file, feed, or API endpoint attached to a dataset package. Its format and URL identify the concrete object an analysis can download.

A reproducible ingestion step records the chosen resource rather than relying only on the human-readable package title.

16961.sourceSearchName: ckan resource metadata ckan resource metadata
16961.title: CKAN Resource Metadata
16961.heading: Document

16962.sourceSearchName: ckan resource metadata ckan resource metadata
16962.title: CKAN Resource Metadata
16962.heading: CKAN Resource Metadata
16962.content:
CKAN resource metadata describes a published resource's URL, format, name, identifier, timestamps, and related properties. Reviewing it helps an analyst choose the correct file and detect changes in a data source.

Metadata should be preserved with the analysis because a stable catalog entry may point to updated content over time.

16963.sourceSearchName: ckan resource metadata ckan resource metadata
16963.title: CKAN Resource Metadata

16965.title: CKAN Package
16965.heading: CKAN Package
16965.content:
A CKAN package is the catalog-level description of a dataset. It groups title, ownership, description, tags, update information, and one or more [[CKAN Resource|resources]] under a stable identifier.

Selecting a package does not by itself select a file, because different formats or vintages may be attached as separate resources.

16967.sourceSearchName: ckan data repository ckan data repository
16967.title: CKAN Data Repository
16967.heading: Document

16968.sourceSearchName: ckan data repository ckan data repository
16968.title: CKAN Data Repository
16968.heading: CKAN Data Repository
16968.content:
A CKAN data repository publishes datasets through a catalog that can be searched by people and accessed programmatically. It separates catalog metadata from the downloadable resources that contain actual records.

An R workflow can use this structure to locate a dataset, inspect its metadata, and retrieve a selected resource reproducibly.

16971.title: Civil GPS Receiver Market
16971.heading: Civil GPS Receiver Market
16971.content: The civil GPS receiver market emerged when open signals, improved microelectronics, and mass production reduced equipment from specialized military hardware to compact commercial devices. Surveyors and marine users formed early high-value markets, followed by hikers, motorists, aircraft operators, and embedded systems. Civil demand also changed policy: widespread economic dependence made intentional degradation or withdrawal of the service increasingly costly even though the constellation remained publicly funded.

16974.title: Circle Equation
16974.heading: Circle Equation
16974.content:
A circle with center $(h,k)$ and radius $r$ consists of the points satisfying

$$(x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2.$$

The equation follows from holding the [[Distance Between Points]] from $(x,y)$ to the center constant. Expanding it gives a general quadratic equation whose equal squared coefficients reflect the circle's symmetry.

16977.sourceSearchName: cinematic bullet hit compositing cinematic bullet hit compositing
16977.title: Cinematic Bullet-Hit Compositing
16977.heading: Cinematic Bullet-Hit Compositing
16977.content: A screen bullet hit follows the visual convention and tone of the production, which may differ from a literal entry wound. The book times a desaturated, darkened burst to the performer's reaction and places a second elongated burst behind the body for an exit effect, using roto to prevent the rear element from crossing in front. A still spray image on a perspective-aligned card can be revealed with a moving soft matte. The composite is built from timed layers rather than one footage overlay. See [[Interactive Light from Muzzle Flashes]] for the related gunfire cue.

16980.title: CIA Triad
16980.heading: CIA Triad
16980.content:
The CIA triad describes information security through [[Information Confidentiality|confidentiality]], [[Data Integrity|integrity]], and [[Information Availability|availability]]. Confidentiality limits disclosure, integrity protects correctness and intended use, and availability makes information or services accessible when needed.

The three properties expose different kinds of failure. A system can keep data secret while allowing unauthorized alteration, or can preserve correct data that users cannot reach in time, so a security requirement should address each property separately.

A CI test stage runs automated tests as part of the source-to-artifact build. Unit and other suitable tests provide evidence before the pipeline publishes a package for release.

The stage acts as a gate only for the checks it actually executes. A passing result means those defined expectations passed for that revision, not that every production behavior is known to be correct.

16986.title: Churn Label Definition
16986.heading: Churn Label Definition
16986.content:
A churn classifier needs a business definition of what counts as a customer leaving. Explicit contract cancellation may be straightforward to label. In a prepaid service, inactivity could mean departure, temporary nonuse, or a delayed top-up, so a time and balance rule must be chosen.

That rule is then encoded to label historic training cases. A model can only learn the event as operationally defined; changing the threshold changes the target and possibly the apparent performance. Label design is therefore a substantive business and data science decision.

16989.sourceSearchName: church turing thesis church turing thesis
16989.title: Church-Turing Thesis
16989.heading: Church-Turing Thesis
16989.content:
The Church-Turing thesis states that anything computable by an [[Algorithm]] can be computed by a [[Turing Machine]]. It treats the Turing machine's simple symbol manipulations as a formal expression of the general notion of effective computation.

It is a thesis rather than a proved mathematical theorem because it relates a formal machine to the informal idea of everything that can be computed. A fundamentally different form of effective computation could disprove it, but no accepted counterexample is known within the source's account.

The computation text motivates the thesis through simulation: ordinary computers, multitape machines, nondeterministic machines, general grammars, and other proposed models can be simulated without increasing which functions and languages are computable.

16990.sourceSearchName: church turing thesis church turing thesis
16990.title: Church-Turing Thesis

16991.heading: Document

16992.sourceSearchName: choropleth class count choropleth class count
16992.title: Choropleth Class Count
16992.heading: Choropleth Class Count
16992.content: Choropleth class count is the number of intervals used in a [[Classed Choropleth]]. More classes retain finer numeric distinctions but demand more difficult color discrimination; fewer classes are legible but may conceal spatial variation. The source recommends a modest range, commonly three to seven classes, as a compromise. The final choice depends on data distribution, palette, map size, and the distinctions the map must support.

16993.sourceSearchName: choropleth class count choropleth class count
16993.title: Choropleth Class Count
16993.heading: References

16995.title: Choropleth Map
16995.heading: Choropleth Map
16995.content: A choropleth map fills geographic regions according to an attribute associated with each polygon. It is most appropriate for rates, proportions, or other normalized values that can be treated as uniform within relatively homogeneous regions. Raw totals often reflect region size or population more than the intended phenomenon. Color may be continuous or classed, and the regional boundaries remain part of the interpretation rather than mere decoration.

16998.title: Chromatic Index
16998.heading: Chromatic Index
16998.content:
The chromatic index of a graph is the minimum number of colors needed for a valid [[Edge Coloring]]. It therefore measures the smallest number of mutually exclusive slots required when adjacent edges cannot receive the same assignment.

For a tournament graph, the chromatic index is the minimum number of days required under the rule that each player can appear in only one match per day. A greedy algorithm can find a valid schedule without always attaining this minimum.

17000.sourceSearchName: choreographing destruction layers choreographing destruction layers

17001.sourceSearchName: choreographing destruction layers choreographing destruction layers
17001.title: Choreographing Destruction Layers
17001.heading: Choreographing Destruction Layers
17001.content: A convincing digital explosion is a timed relationship among fractured structural pieces, fire and smoke, expelled interior debris, and surviving damaged material. The book compares this to a practical set explosion whose different charges are fired in sequence. Showing a whole model until destruction, then swapping to fractured geometry, prevents premature gaps. Fire footage on depth-staged cards can sit behind, between, and in front of fragments; particle-driven debris suggests contents that were inside the destroyed object. See [[Rigid Body Fracture and Collision]] and [[Geometry-Instanced Particle Debris]].

17004.sourceSearchName: choosing features for 2 d tracking choosing features for 2 d tracking
17004.title: Choosing Features for 2D Tracking
17004.heading: Choosing Features for 2D Tracking
17004.content: A reliable track needs a feature that is distinct, contrasted, and visible through the frames being solved. A repeated texture can be confused with another copy of itself; a long straight edge does not uniquely fix movement along that edge; an occluded feature cannot provide continuous evidence. The tracker should preferably be near the depth of the element being attached so parallax does not make the match slide. Choosing the feature well often matters more than enlarging the search region. See [[Tracker Search Window Tuning]].

17007.title: Choosing a Chroma Key Color
17007.heading: Choosing a Chroma Key Color
17007.content: A keying background need not be blue or green. Its color should contrast clearly with the subject's colors so the keyer can separate them, and it should be saturated and lit as evenly as the shoot permits. A costume or object that repeats the screen color is likely to disappear with it. Uneven illumination expands the background's color range and forces a wider key tolerance, increasing the chance that foreground detail is lost. The screen choice therefore shapes the difficulty of the later [[Color-Space Keyer Tolerance]] adjustment.

17010.title: Chopping
17010.heading: Chopping
17010.content:
Chopping discards all digits beyond the retained precision without adjusting the final retained digit.

It is simpler than [[Rounding]] but introduces a one-sided error whose magnitude can approach a full unit in the last retained place. Repeated chopping can create systematic numerical bias.

17013.title: Cholesky Decomposition
17013.heading: Cholesky Decomposition
17013.content:
Cholesky decomposition factors a real [[Positive-Definite Matrix|symmetric positive-definite matrix]] as $A=LL^T$, where $L$ is lower triangular with positive diagonal entries.

The symmetry eliminates the need to store two unrelated triangular factors. Solving $Ax=b$ becomes the successive systems $Ly=b$ and $L^Tx=y$.

17016.sourceSearchName: chinese room argument chinese room argument
17016.title: Chinese Room Argument
17016.heading: Chinese Room Argument
17016.content:
The Chinese room argument challenges the claim that executing a formal program is sufficient for understanding. A person who does not know Chinese could follow rules for transforming Chinese symbols and produce convincing answers without knowing what any symbol means. The room would exhibit correct syntax without semantic understanding.

Applied to AI, the argument distinguishes successful symbol manipulation from intentionality and meaning. Critics respond that understanding might belong to the larger system rather than the person following instructions, or that mental activity itself can be explained computationally. The argument therefore identifies a contested assumption behind claims about [[Artificial General Intelligence]] rather than offering a simple performance test.

17019.title: Children Prop
17019.heading: Children Prop
17019.content:
The React children prop contains the nodes nested inside a component by its consumer. Rendering `children` at a chosen place lets the component provide a reusable surrounding layout while callers supply the inner content.

Function-component typing makes this prop available without requiring every props interface to declare it separately. A page component can therefore own width and title styling while accepting arbitrary nested page content.

17022.title: Child Tasks
17022.heading: Child Tasks
17022.content:
A task created while another task is running is not automatically part of its parent's completion. An attached child, created with the appropriate option, extends the parent's lifetime so the parent does not complete until the child has finished.

Attachment also affects how cancellation and exceptions are observed. Because implicit task hierarchies can surprise callers, structured asynchronous code should make ownership and waiting responsibilities explicit.

17025.sourceSearchName: chi squared profile distance chi squared profile distance
17025.title: Chi-Squared Profile Distance
17025.heading: Chi-Squared Profile Distance
17025.content:
A profile divides a row's occurrence counts by that row's total, so long and short texts can be compared by their relative word usage. Correspondence analysis weights the squared difference between two row profiles by the inverse mass of each column. A difference on a rare attribute therefore contributes more than an equal difference on a common one.

This chi-squared distance is appropriate to the frequency table that begins the analysis. The complete factor-space representation preserves it as Euclidean distance, making otherwise awkward weighted relationships easier to inspect and cluster.

17028.title: Checksum
17028.heading: Checksum
17028.content:
A checksum is a value computed from data and later recomputed or compared to detect whether the data changed. The sender or storage system supplies both the data and an expected value, and the receiver checks whether its result agrees.

Checksums can reveal corruption from storage or a noisy transmission channel and can contribute to integrity checking. The strength and trustworthiness of the scheme depend on its algorithm and on protecting the expected value from the same unauthorized modification.

17031.title: Checkpoint
17031.heading: Checkpoint
17031.content:
A checkpoint is a stored point in a game's progress to which the player returns after a setback. It may be created automatically by the system, visibly marked in the world, or chosen by the player through saving.

Checkpoint placement controls the amount of [[Repetition as Punishment|repetition]] attached to failure. A nearby checkpoint supports focused practice, while a distant one makes previously completed play part of the cost of another attempt.

17034.title: Chebyshev Polynomial
17034.heading: Chebyshev Polynomial
17034.content:
Chebyshev polynomials form a family on $[-1,1]$ defined by $T_n(x)=\cos(n\arccos x)$ and a simple recurrence. Their roots and extrema are distributed unevenly, with greater density near the interval endpoints.

Using those nodes in [[Polynomial Interpolation]] reduces the largest interpolation error and avoids the large endpoint oscillations that equally spaced high-degree interpolation can produce.

17037.title: Chatbot
17037.heading: Chatbot
17037.content:
A chatbot is a conversational program whose primary interface is typed or spoken dialogue. Some chatbots are open-ended social systems, while others are narrow agents that answer questions or complete transactions.

The category describes the interaction form, not a guaranteed level of intelligence. A chatbot may rely on scripted rules, statistical [[Intent Classification]], learned generation, or a combination of these methods.

The Bot Framework project describes a chatbot as a conversational state machine whose framework manages service and channel plumbing. Message activities enter through the bot adapter, language understanding selects an intent, and the bot chooses and sends an appropriate reply.

17040.heading: Characteristic Zero
17040.content:
A ring has characteristic zero when no positive multiple of its multiplicative identity equals zero. The integers, rationals, and reals have characteristic zero.

For an integral domain, characteristic zero means the embedded copy of the integers does not collapse modulo a positive integer.

17043.title: Characteristic Polynomial
17043.heading: Characteristic Polynomial
17043.content:
The characteristic polynomial is $p(\lambda)=\det(A-\lambda I)$. Its degree equals the size of the square matrix, and its roots are the eigenvalues counted with multiplicity.

Its coefficients connect eigenvalues to matrix invariants: the sum of eigenvalues equals the [[Matrix Trace]], while their product is related to the [[Determinant]].

17046.title: Characteristic of a Ring
17046.heading: Characteristic of a Ring
17046.content:
The characteristic of a nontrivial ring with identity is the least positive integer n for which n copies of the identity add to zero, if such an integer exists. If none exists, the characteristic is zero.

It is the additive order of the ring identity and controls how integer arithmetic is represented in the ring.

17049.title: Characteristic Equation
17049.heading: Characteristic Equation
17049.content:
The characteristic equation of a square matrix is $\det(A-\lambda I)=0$. Its roots are the matrix's eigenvalues.

The determinant condition makes the homogeneous system $(A-\lambda I)x=0$ singular, allowing a nonzero eigenvector. Directly forming and solving this equation is practical mainly for small matrices.

17055.title: Character Depth
17055.heading: Character Depth
17055.content:
Character depth is the sense that a game character has coherent motives, traits, relationships, and possible responses beyond a visual stereotype. Depth makes behavior understandable without requiring it to be simple or entirely predictable.

It emerges from alignment among appearance, back story, mechanics, animation, dialogue, and change over time. Contradictions can add complexity when the story acknowledges them; accidental contradictions weaken credibility.

17058.title: Character Silhouette
17058.heading: Character Silhouette
17058.content:
A character silhouette is the outer shape by which a game character can be recognized without interior detail. Different silhouettes let players distinguish behaviors even when color, texture, or facial features are hard to see.

Silhouette matters most when several moving characters share a scene and rapid identification affects choice. Hair, limbs, weapons, shields, and proportions can all make a role legible while reinforcing [[Game Character Design|characterization]].

Only details that support believable action or useful dramatic context need to reach the player. An extensive private history is not a substitute for characterization visible through choices, dialogue, animation, and consequences.

17064.title: Chaotic System
17064.heading: Chaotic System
17064.content:
A chaotic system is deterministic but highly sensitive to its initial conditions. Very small differences in starting state can produce dramatically different later behavior.

Chaotic unpredictability is therefore distinct from a [[Random System]]. A designer may know all the rules of a chaotic system while still being unable to make reliable long-range predictions about its outcomes.

17067.title: Chaos Engineering
17067.heading: Chaos Engineering
17067.content:
Chaos engineering deliberately introduces controlled failures to test whether a live system and its operators behave as expected under stress. Experiments begin with explicit hypotheses and bounded impact, then observe detection, degradation, and recovery.

The purpose is to reveal hidden assumptions before uncontrolled failure does. It requires safeguards, monitoring, and progressively increased scope rather than indiscriminate disruption.

A change-in-estimate criterion retains a candidate confounder when adding it changes the exposure coefficient by more than a chosen relative amount, often ten percent. It focuses on distortion of the target association rather than the confounder's own p-value.

The threshold is a practical rule, not a statistical test for confounding. Its result depends on the coefficient scale and the current model, so substantive knowledge and the broader selection strategy still govern the decision.

17076.heading: Chance and Uncertainty in Play
17076.content:
Chance is deliberate randomization, while uncertainty is the broader condition of not knowing what will happen. Hidden information, another player's choice, variable skill, or a complex system can create uncertainty without random numbers.

Chance supports play when players can still decide how to prepare for, interpret, or respond to its results. If an outcome is random and no decision can affect its meaning or consequences, the player becomes an observer of the draw rather than an agent within it.

17085.title: Chain Map
17085.heading: Chain Map
17085.content:
A chain map between chain complexes is a family of homomorphisms fₙ: Cₙ → C′ₙ that commutes with the differentials. Applying a differential before or after the appropriate f gives the same result.

Because it sends cycles to cycles and boundaries to boundaries, a chain map induces homomorphisms on [[Homology Group]]s. Maps of cochain complexes similarly induce maps on cohomology.

17088.title: Chain Rule
17088.heading: Chain Rule
17088.content:
The chain rule differentiates a composition:

$$(f\circ g)'(x)=f'(g(x))g'(x).$$

It multiplies the outer function's rate of change, evaluated at the inner output, by the inner function's rate of change. In [[Leibniz Notation]], the relationship resembles $dy/dx=(dy/du)(du/dx)$.

17091.title: Chain Complex
17091.heading: Chain Complex
17091.content:
A chain complex is a sequence of modules and homomorphisms ··· → Cₙ₊₁ → Cₙ → Cₙ₋₁ → ··· in which every consecutive composite is zero.

The zero-composite condition makes every [[Boundary in a Chain Complex]] a [[Cycle in a Chain Complex]]. Their quotient is the [[Homology Group]], which measures the failure of the complex to be exact.

17106.title: Certificate Authority
17106.heading: Certificate Authority
17106.content:
A certificate authority is a trusted party that signs digital certificates used to associate an identity with a public cryptographic key. A communicating endpoint can use that signature when deciding whether the presented certificate belongs to a party it should trust.

Certificates help establish an [[Encrypted Communication Channel]], but trust also depends on correct names, validity periods, protected private keys, and an accepted authority chain. A certificate does not authorize every action by the identified party.

Within [[Public Key Infrastructure]], a certificate authority supports the creation, distribution, management, and revocation of certificates that bind identities to public keys. A client authenticates a presented certificate before relying on it during secure-session establishment.
links: TLS Authentication and Secure Remote Access

Centroid linkage clustering represents each cluster by the mean of its member coordinates and compares clusters through the distance between those centroids.

The summary is efficient and intuitive for numerical data, but it can hide cluster spread or shape. Merging changes both centroids, so the sequence need not behave like nearest- or furthest-neighbor linkage.

17112.title: Centripetal Acceleration
17112.heading: Centripetal Acceleration
17112.content: Centripetal acceleration points toward the center of a circular path and has magnitude $a_c=v^2/r=r\omega^2$. It exists even in uniform circular motion because the velocity vector changes direction. A real inward resultant force must supply this acceleration; centripetal force is not an additional force separate from gravity, tension, friction, or another interaction.

17115.title: Central Limit Theorem
17115.heading: Central Limit Theorem
17115.content:
The central limit theorem states that the mean of a sufficiently large random sample is approximately normally distributed around the population mean. Its standard error equals the population standard deviation divided by the square root of the sample size.

The approximation concerns the distribution of the sample mean, not a claim that the population itself is normal. Its adequacy depends on sample size and the underlying distribution, so simulation can test its practical accuracy.

17127.title: Cellular Network
17127.heading: Cellular Network
17127.content:
A cellular network divides a geographic region into small radio coverage areas whose frequencies can be reused at sufficient distance. Low-power phones communicate with nearby base stations rather than one powerful transmitter.

The network tracks subscribers and coordinates movement among cells. This architecture expanded mobile capacity beyond the small number of channels available to earlier car-phone systems.

17130.title: Censoring
17130.heading: Censoring
17130.content:
Censoring occurs when an observation's exact event time is not observed, although the subject is known to remain event-free up to a particular time. Right censoring is common when follow-up ends before the event.

Censored observations still contribute information to the risk set until their censoring times. Survival methods rely on assumptions about how censoring relates to event risk, so systematic loss to follow-up can bias the estimated curve.

17133.title: Cellular Handoff
17133.heading: Cellular Handoff
17133.content:
Cellular handoff transfers an active call or data session from one base station to another as the device moves. The system compares signal conditions and changes the serving cell without ending the connection.

Handoff requires subscriber databases, measurement, signaling, and coordinated switching. It turns many local radio cells into the experience of one continuous mobile network.

A cell-laden hydrogel contains living cells dispersed within a hydrated polymer network. The liquid precursor can be molded or printed into a shape and then gelled to hold cells in a three-dimensional support environment.

Cell density, matrix stiffness, crosslinking conditions, transport distance, and biological ligands jointly determine whether the cells survive and organize.

17139.heading: Cellular Agriculture
17139.content:
Cellular agriculture produces food or consumer materials from cultured cells rather than raising and harvesting an entire animal. It adapts cell expansion, scaffolding, differentiation, and bioreactor methods to products whose requirements differ from medical implants.

The field aims to improve resource use and animal welfare while meeting strict expectations for safety, cost, sensory quality, and scale.

Cell seeding places living cells onto or within a scaffold. Density, uniformity, attachment, cell type, and the route by which cells enter the construct affect later survival and organization.

Too few cells may fail to establish supportive contacts, while excessive density can exhaust nutrients before vascular or perfusion systems are available.

17151.title: Cech Complex
17151.heading: Cech Complex
17151.content:
The Čech complex for elements x₁,…,xₙ is built from localizations of a ring or module at products of those elements. Its terms combine one-element and multiple-element localizations with alternating maps.

The cohomology of this complex computes [[Local Cohomology]] supported in the radical of the generated ideal. It provides a direct localization-based model without first constructing an injective resolution.
